finalText:
Redis dropped at 02:14:07 with a plain connection-refused error, no warning before it — everything was healthy up to that second. That's your root cause.

Once redis was gone, the app fell back to hitting the database directly, which triggered a cache miss storm and 5-second timeouts on every request. The request queue built up nonstop from there — reconnect attempts fired every ~90 seconds (attempts 7 through 12 are visible) and all failed the same way, so redis never came back on its own.

The queue passed its stated max of 500 around 02:29 and kept climbing past 550. At 02:31:44 a worker ran out of memory from the backlog and crashed; the supervisor restarted it, but eight seconds later the whole API was declared unresponsive and the process group was killed — that's the outage.

**Bottom line:** redis at `10.0.0.12:6379` went unreachable at 02:14:07 and stayed unreachable for the whole incident. Nothing backpressured the request queue while it waited, so it grew unbounded for 17 minutes until a worker OOM'd and took the service down at 02:31:52.

Worth checking next: why redis at that address was unreachable, and adding a queue depth cap so this degrades instead of crashing next time.
